To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the onion peeling retrieval method yields water vapour profiles in the 15–45-km altitude range with a mean absolute deviation of less than 5% from corresponding ACE-FTS measurements and that SCIAMACHY data tend to be higher than ACE- FTS data.

we have successfully retrieved water vapour profiles from solar occultations with SCIAMACHY, that we have developed a new retrieval method, that we have compared the retrieved water vapour data to ACE-FTS and ECMWF data, and that the agreement is reasonable.

the new retrieval method yields reasonable water vapour profiles in the altitude range of 15–45 km, that SCIAMACHY data tend to be higher than ACE- FTS data, that SCIAMACHI data are in principal in agreement with ECMWF model data, and that the new retrieval approach is a simple, fast, and robust method to derive water vapours from SCIAMACHHY solar occultation data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new retrieval method for water vapour profiles from solar occultations.
a simple retrieval algorithm for water vapour number densities from solar occultation SCIAMACHY measurements.
the derivation of reliable water vapour profiles from solar occultations of the SCIAMACHY instrument on board ENVISAT.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SCIAMACHy water vapour retrieval method presented here is able to deliver reliable results.

the SCIAMACHy water vapour data are reliable in the altitude range of 20 to 45 km and that the differences to the ACE-FTS and ECMWF water vapour data can be attributed to differences in the retrieval algorithms and the data sets.
SCIAMACHY is able to measure water vapour in the stratosphere and mesosphere with a precision of about 5%.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown the potential of SCIAMACHY to provide reliable water vapour profiles in the upper mesosphere/lower thermosphere.
SCIAMACHY measurements provide reliable water vapour profiles in the altitude region 15–45 with a precision of about 10% and an accuracy of about 5% (systematic error).
SCIAMACHY data agree within about 5–10% with ACE-FTS, which in turn agrees within the same range with ECMWF data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the new onion peeling method provides a robust and reliable way to derive water vapous number density profiles from SCIAMCHAY solar occultation data in the altitude region of 20–45 km.
SCIAMACHY measurements are a useful and valuable addition to the existing data sets.
the SCIAMACHX water vapour profiles have the potential to provide a useful data set for the validation of atmospheric models and satellite data.
